newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta stocks seen lower on political tension.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta stocks seen lower on political tension.

text.p: Jakarta stocks are expected to be lower on Wednesday, with sentiment dampened by riots in several areas in Jakarta and Java island on Tuesday, brokers said.

The U.S. Federal Reserve decision on Tuesday to keep the interest rate steady -- which was expected to help market sentiment in local market -- might only give minor support to buying interest, the brokers said.

"The Fed decision is good news for market. But since the political tension ahead of the May 29 election is increasing, I believe investors would prefer to hold their positions or even sell," one broker with Hongkong-based securities firm said.

On Tuesday, election-related violence hit Indonesia as a riot broke out during election campaigning in central Java and troops fired into the air in Jakarta to disperse thousands of supporters of a Moslem-backed minority party.
The ruling Golkar party was scheduled to campaign on Wednesday in several areas in Jakarta.
Some brokers said they believed the prevailing weak market sentiment will provide a good opportunity to buy stocks.

"Political matters are no longer an issue for many veteran players. I believe whoever has good knowledge about Indonesia will get benefit from this situation. They will pick up good stocks at low prices," one broker with major local firm said.
Brokers said banking stocks such as Bank Negara Indonesia and Bank Danamon were likely to attract market attention based on their fundamentals and prospects.
Cigarette makers Sampoerna and Gudang Garam were likely to come under further selling pressure on perception of weak first quarter results, brokers said.
On Tuesday, the Jakarta composite index rose 0.28 points to close at 652.83 points after touching an intra-day high of 655.81 points.
"I think trading volume will stay small as players will prefer to wait until the end of the election campaign later this week," another broker said.
Ceramics and glass maker Mulia Industrindo topped the active list on bargain hunting, with some 11 million shares traded, brokers said. Mulia rose 50 rupiah to 1,275 rupiah.
Brokers said the rebound in Mulia was attributed to expected improved prices in the float-glass market later this year.
Another float-glass maker Asahimas and conglomerate Bakrie were also up on bargain-hunting, brokers said.
The Jakarta stock exchange suspended trading in small property firm Mas Murni on Wednesday after it became active in late trading on Tuesday, a stock exchange official said.

"We suspended the trading in Mas Murni for the morning session as we are waiting for company's explanation after its share price jumped on Tuesday," the official said. He said the stock was expected to resume trading in the afternoon session.
On Tuesday, Mas Murni Indonesia rose 175 rupiah to close at 825 rupiah on a sudden spurt of active buying near the close due to market talk of a possible take-over, brokers said.
